stem: Which one of the following waterways has more economic and strategic significance?
expl: The "Suez Canal" is one of the world's largest artificial canals built in the Isthmus of Suez in Egypt. Due to the construction of this canal, the distance between Europe and India has been reduced by 7000 km. About 12% of global trade passes through it, representing 30% of all global container traffic annually. It is extremely important waterways because of its strategic location between Red Sea and Mediterranean.

stem: Which of the following Isthmuses has been known as the Devil's Neck'?
expl: An isthmus is a narrow strip of land that connects two large landmasses and separates two water bodies. The Kra Isthmus is located in Southern Thailand and Myanmar in Southeast Asia, as a narrow land belt between the Malay Peninsula and the mainland of Southeast Asia. Because the Kra Isthmus is very narrow and creates a hindrance for ship routes, it got a name like “Devil’s Neck.”

stem: Which one of the following separates Tasmania from Australia?
expl: • The Bass Strait is a narrow water body, about 240–350 km wide, located between mainland Australia (Victoria) and the island of Tasmania. This strait geographically separates the two. • The Great Australian Bight is a vast open bay along the extensive southern coast of Australia; it does not separate any island from the mainland. • The Tasman Sea is a large marginal sea spread between the eastern coast of Australia–Tasmania and New Zealand; its expanse is far wider than the Bass Strait. • The Strait of Megellan is located between the South American mainland and the Tierra del Fuego archipelago; it has no relation to Australia–Tasmania.
